previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old man with a history of CNS lymphoma and diabetes insipidus was admitted for elective high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy as part of reinduction therapy following disease recurrence. He presented in stable condition with only chronic tinnitus and no acute symptoms. He received methotrexate 8 g/m² with standard urinary alkalinization and IV hydration. Leucovorin rescue was initiated 24 hours post-infusion, and methotrexate levels declined appropriately to 0.08 by discharge. His hospital course was complicated by asymptomatic hyponatremia, dropping to 123, attributed to desmopressin use in the setting of high IV fluid volume. Management included holding IV fluids, withholding desmopressin temporarily, and administering IV sodium chloride, leading to improvement in sodium to 130. A Port-a-cath was successfully placed on hospital day 3 for future venous access. He remained neurologically stable, seizure-free, and hemodynamically normal throughout. He was discharged home with instructions to resume all home medications, continue temozolomide, and take sodium bicarbonate prior to next methotrexate dose, with follow-up in two weeks.
